summary: futureImpl.Chain blocks Get forever when the source future is already ready because it doesn't properly complete the destination future. The destination is left in a partially completed state with the internal channel never closed, preventing propagation of chained dependents.
userImpact: Users who chain futures where the source is already ready experience indefinite blocking when calling Get() on the chained future.
rootCause: When source future is already ready, Chain copies value and err directly without calling Set(), leaving the destination future in a partially completed state with the internal channel never closed.
proposedFix: Route the already-ready path through normal completion logic: val, err := ch.GetValueAndError(); f.Set(val, err)
resolutionDetails: The fix routes the already-ready path through Set() to properly close the internal channel and propagate chained dependents.
keyQuote: The fix is to route the already-ready path through the normal completion logic: val, err := ch.GetValueAndError(); f.Set(val, err)
